result.title: Biologically-Inspired Spike Encoding and Optimization for Spiking Neural Networks
result.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer theoretical energy-efficiency advantages over conventional deep networks, but realizing these advantages on vision tasks requires sparse spike representations that naive rate-coding methods fail to provide. We combine biologically motivated spike-encoding schemes with two training improvements: Rouser adaptive-threshold surrogate gradients and Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (K-FAC) second-order optimization. The spike encoding schemes experimented with are rate coding, latency coding, DVS-style delta modulation, and Difference-of-Gaussians (DoG) filtering. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate that biologically inspired encoders yield the largest accuracy gains in capacity-constrained regimes and serve as an effective parameter-efficiency lever. DoG and delta modulation encoders produce significantly sparser spike trains than rate coding. K-FAC yields modest but consistent accuracy improvements over Adam-trained baselines, and Rouser's learnable per-neuron thresholds improve Fashion-MNIST accuracy from 87.37% to 88.13% by enabling homeostatic firing-rate regulation. Biologically grounded pre-processing methods can help close the accuracy gap between SNNs and non-spiking baselines without increasing model size.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 MNIST 与 Fashion-MNIST 上比较 rate、latency、DVS 式 delta 调制和 DoG 滤波等脉冲编码方案，并结合 Rouser 自适应阈值替代梯度与 K-FAC 二阶优化，考察稀疏脉冲表示带来的精度与参数效率收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「输入端稀疏化视觉信息 + 可学习神经元阈值」的设定可作为视觉证据筛选与动态计算分配的远域线索，但任务远小于 VLM 推理，是否可迁移至 latent 状态需较多核查。
